problem_text:
A logistics manager must select cargo containers to load onto a transport aircraft. Available containers are:

* Container 1: weight 47 tons, revenue $226,000
* Container 2: weight 33 tons, revenue $76,000
* Container 3: weight 6 tons, revenue $269,000
* Container 4: weight 3 tons, revenue $293,000
* Container 5: weight 16 tons, revenue $58,000
* Container 6: weight 47 tons, revenue $203,000
* Container 7: weight 24 tons, revenue $280,000
* Container 8: weight 21 tons, revenue $297,000
* Container 9: weight 45 tons, revenue $289,000
* Container 10: weight 26 tons, revenue $167,000
* Container 11: weight 16 tons, revenue $299,000
* Container 12: weight 45 tons, revenue $56,000
* Container 13: weight 10 tons, revenue $217,000
* Container 14: weight 50 tons, revenue $196,000
* Container 15: weight 48 tons, revenue $155,000
* Container 16: weight 23 tons, revenue $268,000
* Container 17: weight 24 tons, revenue $20,000
* Container 18: weight 1 ton, revenue $10,000
* Container 19: weight 10 tons, revenue $141,000
* Container 20: weight 48 tons, revenue $117,000

The aircraft has a maximum payload capacity of 380 tons. Determine which containers to load to maximize total revenue without exceeding this weight limit. Each container must be either fully loaded or left behind.
